```{r, include = FALSE}
  comment = "#>"

```

```{r setup}
library(haufenR)
```

```{r example-data-1}
# --- Example 1: Random Clusters ---

set.seed(123)
# Generate 3 random clusters 
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(50*2, mean = 0), ncol = 2),
           matrix(rnorm(50*2, mean = 3), ncol = 2),
           matrix(rnorm(50*2, mean = 6), ncol = 2))

# Inspect first few rows
head(X)

# Apply k_means from haufenR
res <- k_means(X, K = 3, max_iter = 100, nstart = 5)

# Cluster centers
res$centers

# Cluster assignments
cat("Cluster assignment counts:\n")
table(res$clusters)

# Visualize
plot(X, col = res$clusters, pch = 19, main = "k-means Cluster")
points(res$centers, col = 1:3, pch = 8, cex = 2) # Mark centers
```

```{r example-data-2}
# --- Example 2: Comparison with R's kmeans ---

set.seed(123)
# Apply kmeans from R
res_r <- kmeans(X, centers=3)

par(mfrow = c(1,2)) #Side-by-side plotting

# Visualize own k_mean
plot(X, col = res$clusters, pch = 19, main = "Own k_means")
points(res$centers, col = 1:3, pch = 8, cex = 2)

# Visualize R's built in kmean
plot(X, col = res_r$cluster, pch = 19, main = "R kmeans")
points(res_r$centers, col = 1:3, pch = 8, cex = 2)

# Compare centers
cat("Centers of own implementation:\n")
res$centers
cat("Centers of R's implementation:\n")
res_r$centers #Same centers (with same seed)

par(mfrow = c(1,1)) #Reset plotting

## Our k_means is doing the same as the kmeans-function in R
```

```{r example-data-3}
# --- Example 3: Another dataset---

set.seed(42)
X2 <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(302, mean = 0), ncol = 2),
           matrix(rnorm(502, mean = 5), ncol = 2))
res2 <- k_means(X2, K = 2)

# Plot
plot(X2, col = res2$clusters, pch=19, cex = 0.2)
points(res2$centers, col = 1:2, pch = 8, cex = 2)

```

```{r example-data-4}
# --- Example 4: Edge case with a single point ---

single_point <- matrix(c(1,2), nrow = 1)
res_single <- k_means(single_point, K = 1)

res_single$centers
res_single$clusters

plot(single_point, col = res_single$clusters, pch = 19, main = "k-means Cluster")
points(res_single$centers, col = 1, pch = 8, cex = 2)
```

```{r example-data-5}
# --- Example 5: Demonstrating multiple random starts improves within-cluster of sum squares ---

set.seed(123)
X3 <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(50*2, mean = 0, sd = 1.5), ncol = 2),
           matrix(rnorm(50*2, mean = 2, sd = 1.5), ncol = 2),
           matrix(rnorm(50*2, mean = 4, sd = 1.5), ncol = 2))
res1 <- k_means(X3, K = 3, nstart = 1)
res5 <- k_means(X3, K = 3, nstart = 5)

res1$tot_withinss
res5$tot_withinss

## With multiple random starts the algorithm can find a better clustering solution with a smaller total within-cluster sum of squares
```

```{r example-data-6}
# --- Example 6: Invalid input ---
invalid_X <- matrix(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), ncol = 2)
tryCatch(
  k_means(invalid_X, K = 2),
  error = function(e) message("Caught expected error: ", e$message)
)
```
